newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates stable to a touch higher.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates stable to a touch higher.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were trading at an unchanged to slightly higher level on Friday after the Dutch central bank allocated 2.54 billion guilders to the money market under a four-day special advances pact.
"The allocation was sufficient, but slightly more liquidity would have been welcome as well," said one dealer.
On Thursday the Dutch central bank left the special advances rate unchanged at 2.90 percent.
Call money was bid between 3.06-12 percent.
Other rates were glued to previous levels. Three month deposits were bid at an unchanged 3.12 percent.
Dealers had not noticed any business in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) as prices remained at previous levels.
The June DTC programmes were priced at 3.10 percent and the December contracts at 3.18 percent.
The guilder was a touch stronger versus the German mark at 112.48 per 100 marks from 112.495 on Thursday.
